Batch 1:
PRESS CONFERENCE 20. MAY 2014 Service successes boost foreign trade Current developments in the Austrian balance of payments Likes. Andreas Ittner Deputy Governor Likes. Dr. Johannes Turner Director of the Department of Statistics Page 1 Summary of key developments in 2013  Austria is once again generating solid current account growth. At EUR 8.5 billion or 2.7% of GDP, the surplus once again significantly exceeded the good result of 2012 (EUR 7.3 billion).
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 2:
Austria has so far coped comparatively well with the challenges of the globally unfavourable economic environment and continues to be one of the competitive and macro-economically stable countries. The chemistry between Austria and its trading partners is right. Between 2007 and 2013, chemical products made the main contribution to growth in domestic exports. Food and beverages as well as machinery and vehicles follow at a considerable distance.13% of exports are in the field of cutting-edge technology. Austria's service providers are sailing on a record course.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 3:
At EUR 15.4 billion, the services balance shows a historic record surplus. A high proportion of technology and innovation, which mainly comes from IT, architecture and engineering services, testifies to an increasingly modern orientation of the service sector. The importance of transport, on the other hand, is declining. Tourism industry celebrates the most successful year in its history. Foreign tourists spent more than EUR 15 billion in Austria in 2013, more than ever before.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 4:
In view of a slight decline in Austrians' expenditure on outbound travel, the surplus from the travel balance rose to EUR 7.5 billion, also an unprecedented figure. However, all these successes are not a cushion of peace! Constant efforts are needed to maintain the competitiveness and location quality of the internationally strongly networked domestic economy. Securities business with foreign countries continues to suffer from crisis paralysis. Austria's international investment as well as the financing by means of securities is not gaining momentum. The bond business is stagnating.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 5:
At best, private households are showing certain signs of a revival in view of the renewed interest in investment funds. Eastern Europe, please wait! Austria's direct investment in Central, Eastern and Southeastern Europe collapsed in 2013. The investment volume of EUR 1.5 billion was the lowest since 1999. Only Croatia, the Czech Republic and the Republic of Serbia were able to place among the top ten. In the long term, however, this region will remain interesting for domestic companies.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 6:
In 2013, more than 80% of investments went to the Netherlands, Germany and Norway. Page 2 Development and composition of the current account Balances in billion EUR 15 10 5 0 -5 -10 2006 2007 2008 2009 Goods (left axis) Business-related services (left axis) Current transfers (left axis) Source: OeNB, Statistik Austria. Final data by 2011, revised data in 2012, provisional data in 2013. 2010 2011 2012 Travel (left axis) Income (left axis) Current account (right axis) Chart 1 as % of GDP 5 4 3 2 1 0 -1 -2 -3 2013 Austria's current account is on the upswing In 2013, Austria again achieved a current account surplus: just under EUR 8.5 billion, or 2.7% of GDP. The trade deficit has halved: EUR -3.8 billion. Trade in goods could not escape the weak global growth.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 7:
Exports have developed weakly and imports have declined. The surplus from trade in services reached the highest level ever recorded: EUR 15.4 billion. Both tourism and other commercial service providers - in particular engineering, IT and trade - have now overtaken the previous highs recorded in 2008, before the financial and fiscal crisis. Even if the balance of income streams in the year under review shows a small minus, a positive trend is unmistakable. The persistent surpluses in trade in services continuously reduce foreign debt, which automatically relieves the income balance.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 8:
Page 3 Current account balances as % of GDP within the EU benchmark 12 Euro area 10 Chart 2 other EU countries 8 6 4 2 0 -2 -4 -6 NL DE IE SI LU AT SK MT IT ES GR PT EE FI FR BE CY GB CZ PL RO LV HR LT BG HU SE DK Source: Eurostat. * Moving average over three years. 2011-2013* 2013 Austria is characterised by a stable foreign trade Austria's current account development is within the guideline values of the EU Commission. The surpluses that have been recorded for around ten years have helped to reduce the foreign debt that had previously been built up. The economy of the euro area as a whole emerged from recession in 2013 and is expected to pick up speed in the course of the current year (EU Commission forecast: 1.2%). The external imbalances of the Member States, which had large current account deficits, are gradually improving. The accumulated external debt, on the other hand, is decreasing only slowly.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 9:
The recovery is therefore still fragile and export development requires the support of growth sectors, especially the service sector. Little attention is paid to the major role that foreign corporations play in Austria for foreign trade: 45% of the exports of goods manufacturers and 42% of the exports of services (excluding travel) are accounted for by foreign-controlled companies. Their share is particularly high (more than 50%) in the automotive industry and pharmaceuticals as well as in the innovative areas of research and development as well as computer and information services. Securing the attractiveness of the location is therefore of essential importance for the further development of Austria's current account. You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 10:
Austria's goods export "goes global" In 2013, growth impulses for domestic goods exports came from Russia and the oil-exporting countries of the Middle East. Since the outbreak of the financial crisis, target markets outside the EU have become increasingly important for Austrian industry as a whole. They now account for a third of goods exports. Sales to the BRICS countries1 grew by 9% p.a., to the future markets "Next 11"2 by 5% p.a. and amounted to a total of EUR 13 billion of total export revenues in 2013. The Russian Federation is now one of the ten most important target markets and China is already ranked 11th.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 11:
Growth impulses from the EU in 2013 came mainly from France and the United Kingdom (both 5%). The first signs of an upturn in exports were seen in Hungary (7%), Poland (5%) and Slovenia (8%). Overall, exports of goods recorded low growth in 2013 for the second year in a row (according to the balance of payments 1.1% to around EUR 127 billion). 1 Brazil, Russian Federation, India, China and Hong Kong, South Africa. 2 Egypt, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria, Pakistan, Philippines, Korea, Turkey, Vietnam. Page 5 Evolution of exports of goods by product group 2007 to 2013, growth contributions in % Halbfertigwaren Chart 3 Raw materials, fuels and energy Machinery and vehicles Total exports of goods: 8.6 % Other manufactured goods Food & Beverages Chemical products 0,0 0,5 1,0 1,5 2,0 2,5 3,0 3,5 4,0 Source: Statistik Austria. During the financial crisis, the pharmaceutical industry supported the export trend In 2013, machinery and vehicles, which traditionally form the most important export sector in Austria, recorded the highest growth (4.3% or 2 to EUR 49 billion).
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 12:
However, over the entire period from 2007 to 2013, which was marked by the financial and fiscal crisis, the highest contribution to growth came from the chemical pharmaceutical industry, which proved its resistance to crises. In 2013, their export volume amounted to EUR 16.6 billion, which corresponds to 13.4% of total exports of goods, placing them in third place behind machinery and vehicles as well as semi-finished goods. The export value of all manufactured goods from Austria amounted to EUR 80.2 billion. This corresponds to around two-thirds of total exports. Only 22% was accounted for by semi-finished goods, which are used in the production of consumer or capital goods in other countries.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 13:
The Austrian export structure thus allows a high proportion of global added value generated in the course of production at locations in several countries to be generated domestically. However, it should not be forgotten that domestic suppliers are among the market leaders worldwide, for example in the paper and goods made of mineral materials (building materials, insulation materials, refractory goods). Page 6 Composition of exports of services in industry in % of total Mechanical engineering and vehicle construction Electrical engineering, electronics, optics Other goods Chemicals, plastics, pharmaceuticals Metal & Metal Goods Wood, paper, printing Glass, stoneware Food, beverages, tobacco Textiles, clothing, leather Source: OeNB, Statistik Austria. 0 10 20 30 40 50 60 70 80 Commercial services: legal, tax, management consulting, advertising, market research Network services: transport, communication Other services: including trade, construction, building, directing costs Technical services: R&D, architecture, engineering, IT, license income Chart 4 90 100 Services are the key to success Industry is no longer just an exporter of goods, but also of services. 16% of service exports (around EUR 5.5 billion out of a total of EUR 34 billion in 2013) are accounted for by goods manufacturers, which thus rank 2nd among the leading sectors after the transport sector and even before trade. In order to assert itself against competitors worldwide, no longer individual goods, but system packages are exported and the delivery of goods is enriched with accompanying advice, training, advertising, assembly and repair. In addition to unit prices and the duration of trade settlement, product differentiation is one of the most important competitive factors in goods trading, especially in the technology sectors.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 14:
Accordingly, the mechanical engineering, automotive and electronics sectors in Austria are among the most important service exporters. In addition to engineering and other technical services, research and development services are provided abroad. In these types of services, industry has an export share of more than 50% and thus a higher priority than the corresponding service sectors. While modern information technologies facilitate global market access (e.g. through software downloads or online training), most services are still based on personal interaction between provider and customer, which limits their reach.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 15:
The neighbouring countries and the member states of the EU are therefore the most important target market for the export of services from Austria. A shift in trade in trade in goods in favour of third countries, as can be observed in trade in goods, does not take place in trade in services. On the contrary, the importance of Germany as the most important sales market increased further in 2013: 6% or EUR 0.7 billion to EUR 12.2 billion. You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 16:
Data without travel. Chart 5 in billion EUR 40 35 30 25 20 15 10 5 0 2013 The IT industry drives Austria's exports In contrast to trade in goods, whose growth almost came to a standstill under the sovereign debt crisis in the euro area and the subdued economy in developing and emerging countries, services remained largely unimpressed: exports expanded by 9% in 2012 and by 5% in 2013. This is mainly due to services with a high proportion of innovation and technology. These include IT service providers who develop customer-specific software and offer hardware and network support, but also the offer of architects and engineers. Technical services accounted for 28% of total export revenues in 2013, or EUR 9.4 billion in absolute terms.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 17:
In the long term, the share increased by 15 percentage points. The importance of the most important export category, transport, has decreased in the course of the financial, fiscal and economic crisis and is stagnating in the long term. In addition to a high degree of dependence on economic developments, domestic providers are confronted with competition from low-cost providers from Eastern Europe. The importance of other, traditional types of services such as construction and trade is also declining in the long term. Batch 18:
Final data by 2011, revised data in 2012, provisional data in 2013. Expenditure international passenger transport (left axis) Revenue international passenger transport (left axis) 2013  A record year for the Austrian tourism industry Foreign tourists spent more than EUR 15 billion in Austria in 2013. These are the highest revenues ever generated. In view of a slight decline in Austrians' expenditure on outbound travel, the surplus from the travel balance rose to EUR 7.5 billion, also an unprecedented figure. With almost 25 million arrivals of foreigners, a record result was achieved for the fourth time in uninterrupted order.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 19:
Statistics Austria also recorded a clear increase in overnight stays for foreigners in the 2013 reporting year with 96.8 million overnight stays (1.9%). Only in 1991 and 1992, in the wake of German reunification, had this figure been exceeded. Including domestic guests, 2013 also recorded a historic maximum of 132.6 million overnight stays. In 2012, the IMF ranks Austria 13th in terms of tourism revenues: only the USA, China and the major European destinations, as well as Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and Australia are ahead of Austria. Countries such as India, Canada, Japan or Switzerland have lower tourism revenues than Austria.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 20:
Page 10 Austria's bilateral travel balance with European partners Ratio of exports: imports for 2013 Chart 9 High surplus 3:1 Moderate excess 1:1 Moderate deficit 1:1 High deficit 1:3 Japan USA China Source: OeNB. Provisional data in 2013. The recipe for success: retaining regular guests and opening up new markets Two-thirds of the increase in overnight stays in 2013 was attributable to German guests (1.2 million overnight stays). Contrary to the long-term trend, their share increased in the year under review. There were declining overnight stays not only among guests from the crisis-ridden countries of the Mediterranean (Italy, Spain, Cyprus, Greece), but also among guests from France, the Netherlands or Ireland.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 21:
The double-digit growth in the number of overnight stays by guests from Central and South-Eastern Europe over a long period of time has slowed noticeably (Slovenia 7.7%, Slovakia 6.0%, Czech Republic 1.2%, Poland 1.1%) and has occasionally also turned in the opposite direction (Hungary -0.2%, Romania -3.4%, Croatia -6.0%). Emerging economies show the strongest momentum: the World Tourism Organization reports that travel spending by Chinese and Russians has increased by 25-30% within a year. The Austrian overnight stay statistics recorded the strongest relative increases among guests from Korea (30%), the Arab world (20%), China (14%), as well as Russia, CIS and Ukraine (10%). Meanwhile, the number of overnight stays of Chinese guests (580,000) exceeds that of guests from Japan. Russia was the eighth most important country of origin in 2013 with almost 2 million overnight stays (well ahead of the USA and France).
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 22:
Page 11 The development of the (primary) income balance Net by type of income in billion EUR 8 Chart 8 6 4 2 0 -2 -4 -6 2000 2001 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 Income from direct investment i.w.S Income from other investments Source: OeNB. Income Balance Final data by 2011, revised data in 2012, provisional data in 2013. 2007 2008 2009 2010 Income from portfolio investments Earned income 2011 2012 2013 Better asset position leads to balance of income balance Thanks to the reduction of Austria's debt abroad, Austria's income balance is also improving steadily: up to and including 2007 it showed a structural deficit, sincethen the surpluses predominate. Negative contributions are mainly made by interest on the national debt held abroad, while earned income and interest income from loans and deposits (almost always) show a surplus of revenue. Themost important change concerns income from direct investment, where Austria has become a net investor since the opening up to the East and accession to the EU and has been generating net income on an ongoing basis since 2006. The fact that the income balance for 2013 nevertheless closes with a minus is the result of a "cautious" earnings estimate for direct investment.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 23:
Final results for direct investment returns are always only available with a significant time delay. The OeNB assumes that the extraordinarily high earnings of 2012 will not be repeated in 2013. The declining surpluses in earned income are no cause for concern: the comparatively good employment situation in Austria leads to a growing attractiveness of Austria for cross-border commuters and seasonal workers. Final data by 2011, revised data in 2012, provisional data in 2013. Chart 9 Net foreign investment in Austria in billion EUR 140 120 100 80 60 40 20 0 -20 -40 2001 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 2008 2009 2010 2011 2012 2013 Other investments Net Capital movements with foreign countries continue to gain little momentum Austria's cross-border capital movements are still far from showing the dynamism that characterised it before the outbreak of the financial crisis. Compared to the previous year, however, a certain revival at a low level can be seen in some cases. After all, Austria's net investments were clearly up in 2013: direct investors invested EUR 10.5 billion abroad, securities investments amounted to EUR 2.4 billion. Loan and deposit receivables, on balance, were reduced by EUR 4 billion.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 25:
Foreign investors withdrew a total of EUR 0.1 billion from Austria in 2013, significantly less than in 2012 (EUR -6.3 billion). An increase in foreign direct and portfolio investments was offset by higher divestments in the lending and deposit business. Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 26:
From 2009 onwards, Austria invested mainly in equity securities such as shares and investment certificates, while it was not until 2013 that institutional investors were again increasingly buying bonds abroad. The banking sector was heavily involved in both investment and financing abroad before the crisis, but is now increasingly withdrawing from international markets. From 2009 to 2013, foreign financing through bonds was reduced by more than EUR 40 billion. Bond financing has generally declined since the crisis. In addition to the withdrawal of the banking sector, there were also sharp declines in money market securities.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 27:
However, non-financial companies in particular were able to successfully finance themselves abroad during the entire crisis. The state has always financed itself stably from abroad. Only in 2009 was there a short-term shift from foreign to domestic financing. Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 28:
In 2013, there were positive transactions of EUR 1.8 billion for domestic funds and EUR 1.2 billion for foreign funds. Since 2011, there has been a clear upward trend in the purchase of certificates. Domestic funds were sold to a high degree by the Austrian household sectorduring the crisis, while foreign funds continued to be bought, albeit only slightly. In particular, those funds that invest in short- and long-term interest-bearing securities were removed from household portfolios. Domestic funds are comparatively important for Austrian investors and therefore benefit disproportionately from the current upward trend.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 29:
Overall, the portfolio of foreign funds - especially equity funds - rose by 16% year-on-year to just under EUR 10 billion at the end of 2013. By contrast, ownership of domestic funds rose by only 5% to EUR 39 billion. Active and passive direct investment flows (excluding real estate and special purpose vehicles) wereat an average level of EUR 101/2 billion and EUR 81/2 billion respectively in 2013.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 30:
This is all the more true when one takes into account that it includes a transaction of EUR 3 billion via a regional 'bridgehead'. However, Austrian investments in Central, Eastern and South-Eastern Europe fell significantly in 2013. The investment volume of EUR 1.5 billion was the lowest since 1999. Only Croatia, the Czech Republic and the Republic of Serbia were able to place among the top ten. More than 80% of investments in 2013 went to the Netherlands, Germany and Norway.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 31:
The withdrawal of the Verbundgesellschaft from Turkey, which has exchanged its still young investments in Turkey for power plants in Germany, made a significant contribution to this result. The record investments in Norway are due to OMV's increased efforts to extract crude oil in the North Sea. In addition to energy suppliers, banks, insurance companies and real estate investors as well as mechanical engineering companies invested abroad in 2013. Passive direct investment in 2013 came mainly from Russia, Germany, Luxembourg and Hungary. From an industry perspective, the telecommunications sector, the automotive sector, mechanical engineering, banks and trading companies stand out.
You are a helpful assistant.

Batch 32:

Income from foreign owners also reached historic highs of EUR 9.3 billion. Although dividend payments in 2013 were about 10% lower than in 2012, 2013 should also bring good returns for most investors.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 33:
The OeNB anticipates declining active and rising passive income. Looking at a 10-year period, Austria's active direct investment generated EUR 961/2 billion in profits. The subsidiaries were particularly successful in the Czech Republic, followed by Germany, Switzerland, China and Russia. Page 17 September makes everything new The global economy is subject to constant change. Therefore, it is necessary to adjust the statistics from time to time.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 34:
In 2009, in addition to the new system of national accounts, the IMF also adopted new rules on the compilation of the balance of payments and the international asset position. After the USA, Canada and Australia have already changed their statistics, European economic statistics will now also be put on this new basis in September this year. The new statistics will provide more detail in strategically important areas such as research and development. It contains more detailed rules on the treatment of "contract processing", which is becoming increasingly important in the course of the progressive global division of labour. Statistical systems are better coordinated (GDP generation, use, distribution, financing, external accounts, balance sheet, changes in assets) and comparability between different countries should also improve.
You are a helpful assistant.

Summarize the following excerpt:

Batch 35:
The OeNB does not expect any dramatic changes in the Austrian current account, but shifts within the performance area will result in noticeable changes in individual subheadings. In order to be able to continue to analyse changes over time, the OeNB will offer a complete retrospective calculation for the years from 2006 onwards. Particularly important aggregates are to be recalculated by 1995. Finally, the OeNB would like to thank all the reporters who contribute to the preparation of the balance of payments  in addition to banks and insurance companies about 5,000 large and small companies but also thousands of households  for their cooperation.
